liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Shakedown Street** (6 reviews): The opener is described as amazing, setting a fiery tone for the performance; Garcia plays a high-speed torrent of notes, leading to a new weave with Weir [12][14][16][17][20][22]
- **Passenger** (5 reviews): The performance of this song is highlighted as a standout moment; Described as probably the best and most powerful version heard to date [14][15][18][20][23]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): The performance of this song is noted for exploding on impact [12]

## The recordings

- **gd79-10-25.set1aud-set2sbd.miller.22792.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 165 min; rated 4.65/5 by 31 [1]
- **gd1979-10-25.145460.fob.nak700.rolfe.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 169 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd1979-10-25.152436.senn.blend.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 168 min [6]
- **gd79-10-25.sbd.set2.fishman.21271.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 10 songs; 100 min; rated 4.6/5 by 43 [9]. Said about its sound: Crisp sound features prominent, razzed-up funky organ from Brent, seemingly replacing Weir; The recording is characterized by great crisp sound quality; Sound quality is rated very strong, though the first set lacks this clarity [14][15][17][18][20][22]

## Around the show

- Playful, off-mic stage banter and teases occurred during the lead-in [17]
- The second set is called the hottest found to date, beating all expectations [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd79-10-25.set1aud-set2sbd.miller.22792.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Set 1 Steve Rolfe; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard and Audience composite [1]. Also: Steve Rolfe sent CDs that sounded better, prompting a re-patch of the SBD [1]
- **gd1979-10-25.145460.fob.nak700.rolfe.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Steve Rolfe; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Steve Rolfe's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony D5 [3]. Also: Rob Eaton and Charlie Miller provided a Sennheiser blend source for a Drums patch [3]
- **gd1979-10-25.152436.senn.blend.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Recorded and Transferred by Rob Eaton; transferred by Rob Eaton, Scott Clugston; source: Rob Eaton's Master Audience Cassettes; (2) Sennheiser 441 (left + right) + (1) Sennheiser 421 (center) blend > Nakamichi 550 [6]. Also: Steve Rolfe's Nakamichi 700 source supplied patches for Drums and Space [6]
- **gd79-10-25.sbd.set2.fishman.21271.sbefail.shnf**: source: Soundboard [9]. Also: The reviewer previously owned a poor-quality Maxell cassette copy of the show; Set 2 lineage: SBD to Cassette Master, then DAT, CD, and SHN; The DAT was transferred to CD-r in 1998 [9][19]

## Art and photos

- Poster by David Franklin_Perkins Grateful Dead: [1979-10-25 Veterans' Memorial Coliseum, New Haven, CT, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1979-10-25-veterans-memorial-coliseum-new-haven-ct-usa/) [27]
